title: Australia employer sponsored visa 2026 guide
metaDescription: Australia employer sponsored visa 2026: how sponsorship works, approved sponsors, skilled occupation lists, English and salary rules, and the path to residence.
headline: Australia employer sponsored visa 2026: how sponsorship works

sections.title: What an employer sponsored visa is
sections.content:
An employer sponsored visa lets an approved Australian employer sponsor a skilled worker for a job that cannot easily be filled locally. The employer must first be approved as a sponsor, nominate a specific position, and show the role is genuine and paid at the market salary rate. The worker then applies for the visa linked to that nomination.

Australia's main temporary sponsored route is the Skills in Demand visa, which replaced the Temporary Skill Shortage visa, alongside permanent employer nomination options. Exact occupation lists, salary thresholds and English levels change over time, so always check the current Department of Home Affairs rules before applying.

sections.title: What employers and workers must prove
sections.content:
Employers must show they are lawfully operating, meet sponsorship obligations and, where required, have tested the local labour market. The nominated occupation must be on the relevant skilled list, and the salary must meet both the market rate for the role and any government-set threshold for the visa stream.

Workers must show they have the skills, qualifications or experience for the nominated occupation, meet health and character requirements, and meet the English standard for their stream. Some occupations also need a formal skills assessment before the visa can be granted.

sections.title: From temporary sponsorship to permanent residence
sections.content:
Many sponsored workers start on a temporary visa and later move to permanent residence through employer nomination, once they have worked for their sponsor for the required period and still meet the occupation, salary and English rules. The timing depends on the stream, the occupation and any changes to the rules.

Because sponsorship ties your visa to an employer, changing jobs usually requires a new nomination, so read your conditions carefully. If a sponsorship ends, act quickly: you may have a limited period to find a new sponsor, switch visas or leave Australia, and getting migration advice early protects your options.

faqs.q: How do I get employer sponsorship for Australia?
faqs.a: You need a job offer from an Australian employer that is approved, or willing to become approved, as a sponsor, in an occupation on the relevant skilled list. The employer nominates your position and salary, and you then apply for the visa linked to that nomination. Without a genuine sponsor, an application will not succeed.

faqs.q: Do I need a skills assessment for a sponsored visa?
faqs.a: It depends on your occupation and visa stream. Many trades and professional occupations require a formal skills assessment, while others rely on qualifications and work experience assessed during the nomination. Check the current rules for your exact occupation before lodging, because a missing assessment is a common reason for delays and refusals.

faqs.q: Can a sponsored visa lead to permanent residence?
faqs.a: Yes, many temporary sponsored workers later gain permanent residence through employer nomination after working for their sponsor for the required period. You must still meet the occupation, salary, English, health and character requirements at that stage. Rules and waiting periods change, so confirm the current pathway for your stream before making long-term plans.
